newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fischer to cut short Japan visit due to landslide.
newsitem.headline: Fischer to cut short Japan visit due to landslide.

text.p: Australia's Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Thursday he plans to cut short a trade promotion trip to Japan to visit the site of a landslide that may have killed up to 20 people in Australia's Snowy Mountains.
"I think the priority is the rescue effort," he said. "The state emergency services, the police, and, if the need arises, the defence forces are there."
Fischer said he would attend ministerial talks on Friday and return to Australia on Saturday, cancelling a scheduled climb of Mount Fuji.

Two ski lodges at Thredbo, Australia's most popular ski resort, were crushed by a landslide just before midnight on Wednesday and rescuers at the site on Thursday said there were no signs of life in the ruins.
Fischer said he heard about the disaster on Thursday morning and expressed sympathy for the families of the 20 people thought to have been trapped in the two lodges.

"I wish Godspeed to the rescue effort. I understand the complexity and the challenge represented by the very fragile situation on the side of the mountain," he said. "Let me say that the very famous spirit of the Snowy Mountains will help in the recovery situation."
